pool:
Read static robot knowledge or the latest published calibration without motion. default returns briefing, original URDF, supplemental physical parameters and native geometry reference; named sections return their detailed records. calibration does not capture a new frame. resources lists file IDs; resource returns an actor-readable file reference for client.artifact. geometry_image returns an illustrative image, not a measured scene. Unknown robots/resources return unavailable. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"section":"resources"} ; {"resource_id":"geometry_model","section":"resource"}
Input field guide (use only fields applicable to the selected mode/kind):
input: Type: object. Object rules: section is one of ["default","kinematics","geometry","dynamics","control","hardware","all","calibration","geometry_image","resources","resource"] when supplied; only declared fields.
section: Optional default (default), kinematics, geometry, dynamics, control, hardware, all, calibration, geometry_image, resources or resource. all returns numerical sections and hardware; resource selects a file, resources lists IDs. Type: string; Allowed: ["default","kinematics","geometry","dynamics","control","hardware","all","calibration","geometry_image","resources","resource"].
robot_id: Optional robot ID; omission selects this run's robot. Another robot's current-episode calibration is unavailable. Type: string.
resource_id: Required only for section=resource: copy an ID from section=resources. Omit for every other section. Type: string.

pool:
Read saved permitted RGB and capture-time measured state/calibration without advancing simulation. Returns images, observation_is_current and separately identified current budget. Optional image_delivery ('none', 'focus_roi', 'head_only', 'all') controls image transport; optional focus_3d projects a 3D target_m (env_origin m) or object_id sphere to 1:1 native-sensor crops with crop_xywh_px=[crop_x,crop_y,w,h], projected_center_uv_px and full_uv = [crop_x + local_u, crop_y + local_v]. Manual camera_id selects one view and roi/scale crop or enlarge it while recording the pixel transform (mutually exclusive with focus_3d). Historical frames remain historical; full repeats saved geometry metadata. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"camera_id":"cam_head","observation_id":"obs_1","roi":[100,100,80,60],"scale":2} ; {"focus_3d":{"cameras":["cam_head","cam_right_wrist"],"target_m":[0.0,-0.35,0.8]},"observation_id":"obs_1"}
Input field guide (use only fields applicable to the selected mode/kind):
input: Type: object. Object rules: image_delivery is one of ["none","focus_roi","head_only","all"] when supplied; detail is one of ["summary","full"] when supplied; requires observation_id; only declared fields; all of (must not satisfy (requires focus_3d, roi) | if (image_delivery equals "focus_roi"; requires image_delivery), then (requires focus_3d) | must not satisfy (image_delivery is one of ["none","head_only","all"]; requires focus_3d, image_delivery) | must not satisfy (scale does not equal 1; requires focus_3d, scale) | if (image_delivery is one of ["none","all"]; requires image_delivery), then (must not satisfy (at least one of (requires roi | requires focus_3d | requires camera_id | scale does not equal 1; requires scale))) | if (image_delivery equals "head_only"; requires image_delivery), then (must not satisfy (at least one of (requires focus_3d | camera_id does not equal "cam_head"; requires camera_id)))).
observation_id: ID of a saved permitted observation. Physical actions require the latest current observation in this episode; copy the returned observation_id, never invent one. Type: string.
camera_id: Camera ID present in the selected observation, such as cam_head or cam_right_wrist. Optional unless manual roi is supplied or scale differs from 1; omit with image_delivery='none'/'all', or use focus_3d.cameras for 3D multi-view crops. Type: string.
roi: Original-image integer pixels [x,y,width,height], fully in bounds; use the recorded crop transform to convert enlarged-image coordinates. Optional manual pixel crop; requires camera_id and positive width/height, and is mutually exclusive with focus_3d and image_delivery='none'/'all'. Type: array; Minimum items: 4; Maximum items: 4.
roi[]: Type: integer.
scale: Optional integer enlargement 1..4, default 1. A value other than 1 requires camera_id and cannot be combined with focus_3d or image_delivery='none'/'all'; changes displayed pixels, not source geometry. Type: integer; Minimum (inclusive): 1; Maximum (inclusive): 4.
image_delivery: Optional visual delivery policy: 'none' (0 images; fast numeric state/budget refresh without sensor image transport), 'focus_roi' (1:1 native-sensor local crops around focus_3d; requires focus_3d), 'head_only' (deliver only cam_head RGB image, skipping wrist images), or 'all' (deliver all calibrated camera RGB views, bypassing adaptive view skipping). Omission uses focus_roi when focus_3d is supplied, single-view crop when camera_id/roi is supplied, or the run's standard observation image policy. Type: string; Allowed: ["none","focus_roi","head_only","all"].
focus_3d: Optional 3D-to-2D back-projected native-resolution local ROI request in the env_origin frame; mutually exclusive with manual pixel roi and scale!=1. Supply target_m (3-element [x,y,z] in m) and/or detected 3D object_id (1..64 characters, such as 'o2'). Projects the 3D sphere (center target_m, radius radius_m in m, range 0.02..0.40, default 0.08) through calibrated K/D and measured T_world_camera (including live wrist-camera joint FK) and crops 1:1 native sensor pixels (patch_px 128..480, default 256) without downscale-upscale blur. Returns focus_3d.views[] with crop_xywh_px=[crop_x,crop_y,w,h], projected_center_uv_px=[u,v], local_center_uv_px=[local_u,local_v], full_uv_offset_px=[crop_x,crop_y] and pixel_transform; convert any pixel [local_u,local_v] picked on a returned crop back to original full-image coordinates via full_uv = [crop_x + local_u, crop_y + local_v] for direct use in geometry_query (triangulate / pixel_plane). Type: object. Object rules: only declared fields; at least one of (requires target_m | requires object_id).
focus_3d.target_m: Optional 3-element 3D target center [x, y, z] in env_origin metres (m). Required when object_id is omitted; when both target_m and object_id are supplied, this explicit target_m is used verbatim without background override. Type: array; Minimum items: 3; Maximum items: 3.
focus_3d.target_m[]: Type: number.
focus_3d.object_id: Optional detected 3D object ID (1..64 characters, such as 'o2') from the current or latest permitted 3D observation in this episode. Resolves the object's 3D centre_m (in env_origin m) when target_m is omitted, and resolves an adaptive 3D bounding-sphere radius clamped to 0.02..0.40 m when radius_m is omitted. Type: string; Minimum characters: 1; Maximum characters: 64.
focus_3d.radius_m: Optional 3D sphere radius of interest around the target center in metres (m), range 0.02..0.40, default 0.08 (or the object's 3D bounding-sphere radius clamped to 0.02..0.40 when object_id is supplied and radius_m is omitted). Explicit values are respected verbatim. Type: number; Default: 0.08; Minimum (inclusive): 0.02; Maximum (inclusive): 0.4.
focus_3d.cameras: Optional ordered list of 1..3 unique calibrated camera IDs (each at least 1 character) to crop (e.g. ['cam_head', 'cam_right_wrist']). When omitted (and top-level camera_id is omitted), automatically selects at most 2 frustum-visible cameras closest to the 3D target (preferring the closest visible wrist camera plus cam_head for stereo coverage). Type: array; Minimum items: 1; Maximum items: 3; Unique items: true.
focus_3d.cameras[]: Nonempty calibrated camera ID string (at least 1 character). Type: string; Minimum characters: 1.
focus_3d.patch_px: Optional minimum reference side length in native sensor pixels (px) for the local crop box, range 128..480, default 256. Crops 1:1 from the original full-resolution sensor image (display_scale=1, never downscaled then upscaled) and clamps [x, y, width, height] strictly within sensor bounds. Type: integer; Default: 256; Minimum (inclusive): 128; Maximum (inclusive): 480.
detail: Optional summary/full. Omission uses the actor's configured display default (normally summary) or full for program calls; full repeats original evidence/metadata. Type: string; Allowed: ["summary","full"].

pool:
Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"cam_head","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}
Input field guide (use only fields applicable to the selected mode/kind):
input: Type: object. Object rules: requires request; only declared fields.
request: Required query object with kind and the applicable fields in the tool description's input field guide. Distances use env_origin metres; pixels use original saved images. The gateway supplies episode identity; do not supply hidden state. Type: object. Object rules: exactly one of (kind equals "fk"; requires kind, camera_id; at least one of (requires observation_id | requires observation_ids) | kind equals "camera_pose"; requires kind, camera_id; at least one of (requires observation_id | requires observation_ids) | kind equals "pixel_ray"; requires kind, camera_id, pixel; at least one of (requires observation_id | requires observation_ids) | kind equals "pixel_plane"; requires kind, camera_id, pixel, plane_origin_m, plane_normal, observation_id; only declared fields | kind equals "ray_surface"; requires kind, camera_id, pixel, scene_version, entity_id; at least one of (requires observation_id | requires observation_ids) | kind equals "project_points"; requires kind, camera_id, points_m; at least one of (requires observation_id | requires observation_ids) | kind equals "project_geometry"; requires kind, camera_id; at least one of (requires observation_id | requires observation_ids); all of (at least one of (requires points_m | requires scene_version)) | kind equals "preview_ee"; requires kind, camera_id, action; at least one of (requires observation_id | requires observation_ids) | kind equals "sparse_track"; tracking_method is one of ["lk","sift"] when supplied; requires kind, camera_id; if pixels_a is present, requires pixels_b; if pixels_b is present, requires pixels_a; at least one of (requires observation_id | requires observation_ids) | kind equals "triangulate"; tracking_method is one of ["lk","sift"] when supplied; requires kind, camera_id; if pixels_a is present, requires pixels_b; if pixels_b is present, requires pixels_a; at least one of (requires observation_id | requires observation_ids) | kind equals "build_scene"; tracking_method is one of ["lk","sift"] when supplied; primitive is one of ["plane","box"] when supplied; requires kind, camera_id, base_scene_version; if pixels_a is present, requires pixels_b; if pixels_b is present, requires pixels_a; at least one of (requires observation_id | requires observation_ids) | kind equals "alignment"; requires kind, camera_id, scene_version; if points_m is present, requires pixels; if pixels is present, requires points_m; at least one of (requires observation_id | requires observation_ids) | kind equals "help"; requires kind | kind equals "batch" when supplied; requires queries; only declared fields | kind is one of ["compare_regions","depth_points","forget_target","grasp_candidates","place_candidates","refresh_target","region_geometry","register_target","skill_help","target_status"]; requires kind). Type: object.
request.kind: [request.kind="alignment" or request.kind="batch" or request.kind="build_scene" or request.kind="camera_pose" or request.kind="fk" or request.kind="help" or request.kind="pixel_plane" or request.kind="pixel_ray" or request.kind="preview_ee" or request.kind="project_geometry" or request.kind="project_points" or request.kind="ray_surface" or request.kind="sparse_track" or request.kind="triangulate"] Required: help, camera_pose, fk, pixel_ray, pixel_plane, project_points, preview_ee, triangulate, sparse_track, build_scene, ray_surface, project_geometry, alignment or batch. RGB-D kinds follow depth_query when enabled. RGB-D compatibility kinds, only when enabled. Use depth_query for the complete field contract, units and bounds; these requests are forwarded to the same depth owner for validation. [request.kind="fk"] Type: string; Value: "fk". [request.kind="camera_pose"] Type: string; Value: "camera_pose". [request.kind="pixel_ray"] Type: string; Value: "pixel_ray". [request.kind="pixel_plane"] Type: string; Value: "pixel_plane". [request.kind="ray_surface"] Type: string; Value: "ray_surface". [request.kind="project_points"] Type: string; Value: "project_points". [request.kind="project_geometry"] Type: string; Value: "project_geometry". [request.kind="preview_ee"] Type: string; Value: "preview_ee". [request.kind="sparse_track"] Type: string; Value: "sparse_track". [request.kind="triangulate"] Type: string; Value: "triangulate". [request.kind="build_scene"] Type: string; Value: "build_scene". [request.kind="alignment"] Type: string; Value: "alignment". [request.kind="help"] Type: string; Value: "help". [request.kind="batch"] Type: string; Value: "batch". Type: string; Allowed: ["compare_regions","depth_points","forget_target","grasp_candidates","place_candidates","refresh_target","region_geometry","register_target","skill_help","target_status"].
request.observation_id: Required for single-view kinds: saved calibrated observation ID. [request.kind="alignment" or request.kind="batch" or request.kind="build_scene" or request.kind="camera_pose" or request.kind="fk" or request.kind="pixel_plane" or request.kind="pixel_ray" or request.kind="preview_ee" or request.kind="project_geometry" or request.kind="project_points" or request.kind="ray_surface" or request.kind="sparse_track" or request.kind="triangulate"] Type: string; Minimum characters: 1.
request.observation_ids: For tracking/triangulation/build_scene: [before_id,after_id] sharing calibration and reference frame; same ID with two cameras is allowed. For alignment: held-out observation IDs, excluding scene training frames. [request.kind="alignment" or request.kind="build_scene" or request.kind="camera_pose" or request.kind="fk" or request.kind="pixel_ray" or request.kind="preview_ee" or request.kind="project_geometry" or request.kind="project_points" or request.kind="ray_surface" or request.kind="sparse_track" or request.kind="triangulate"] Type: array; Minimum items: 1.
request.observation_ids[]: [request.kind="alignment" or request.kind="build_scene" or request.kind="camera_pose" or request.kind="fk" or request.kind="pixel_ray" or request.kind="preview_ee" or request.kind="project_geometry" or request.kind="project_points" or request.kind="ray_surface" or request.kind="sparse_track" or request.kind="triangulate"] Type: string; Minimum characters: 1.
request.camera_id: Required except help: camera in the first/selected observation. [request.kind="alignment" or request.kind="batch" or request.kind="build_scene" or request.kind="camera_pose" or request.kind="fk" or request.kind="pixel_plane" or request.kind="pixel_ray" or request.kind="preview_ee" or request.kind="project_geometry" or request.kind="project_points" or request.kind="ray_surface" or request.kind="sparse_track" or request.kind="triangulate"] Type: string; Minimum characters: 1.
request.frame_id: Optional reference frame; defaults to the observation calibration frame (normally env_origin) and must match it. [request.kind="alignment" or request.kind="build_scene" or request.kind="camera_pose" or request.kind="fk" or request.kind="pixel_plane" or request.kind="pixel_ray" or request.kind="preview_ee" or request.kind="project_geometry" or request.kind="project_points" or request.kind="ray_surface" or request.kind="sparse_track" or request.kind="triangulate"] Type: string; Minimum characters: 1.
request.pixel: Required for pixel_ray/pixel_plane/ray_surface: [u,v] original-image pixels, inside the image; ray depth alone remains unknown. [request.kind="pixel_plane" or request.kind="pixel_ray" or request.kind="ray_surface"] Type: array; Minimum items: 2; Maximum items: 2.
request.pixel[]: [request.kind="pixel_plane" or request.kind="pixel_ray" or request.kind="ray_surface"] Type: number.
request.plane_origin_m: Required only for pixel_plane: an explicit [x,y,z] point on your hypothesized infinite plane, in calibration-frame metres (normally env_origin). No default surface height or object depth is supplied; an intersection is not an observed object surface. [request.kind="pixel_plane"] Type: array; Minimum items: 3; Maximum items: 3.
request.plane_origin_m[]: [request.kind="pixel_plane"] Type: number.
request.plane_normal: Required only for pixel_plane: finite nonzero [nx,ny,nz] plane normal in the calibration frame; normalized by the tool. The selected pixel is assumed to lie on this plane. Absolute normal dot ray below 0.01, or intersection at/behind the camera, returns unknown/null. Result ray_plane_condition_factor is 1/abs(dot) and d_point_d_normal_offset_m is the [dx,dy,dz] shift of point_m per +1 m plane shift along this normal. [request.kind="pixel_plane"] Type: array; Minimum items: 3; Maximum items: 3.
request.plane_normal[]: [request.kind="pixel_plane"] Type: number.
request.plane_origin_alt_m: Optional only for pixel_plane: a second [x,y,z] point for the same caller-supplied plane normal. The tool returns alternate_point_m, alternate_ray_distance_m and assumption_delta_m so you can see how the plane hypothesis changes the result; it does not select a default or measure the surface. If either intersection is near-parallel, nonfinite or behind the camera, the query returns unknown/null. [request.kind="pixel_plane"] Type: array; Minimum items: 3; Maximum items: 3.
request.plane_origin_alt_m[]: [request.kind="pixel_plane"] Type: number.
request.target_camera_id: Optional only for pixel_plane: saved calibrated camera in the same observation (such as a wrist view) on which to project point_m (and optional alternate_point_m) and return a geometry overlay image in the same call. [request.kind="pixel_plane"] Type: string; Minimum characters: 1.
request.scene_version: Required for ray_surface/alignment and project_geometry without explicit points_m: existing explicitly reconstructed local scene version. Never a hidden native scene. Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"cam_head","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}

pool.description: Required only for pixel_plane: an explicit [x,y,z] point on your hypothesized infinite plane, in calibration-frame metres (normally env_origin). No default surface height or object depth is supplied; an intersection is not an observed object surface.

Required only for pixel_plane: finite nonzero [nx,ny,nz] plane normal in the calibration frame; normalized by the tool. The selected pixel is assumed to lie on this plane. Absolute normal dot ray below 0.01, or intersection at/behind the camera, returns unknown/null. Result ray_plane_condition_factor is 1/abs(dot) and d_point_d_normal_offset_m is the [dx,dy,dz] shift of point_m per +1 m plane shift along this normal.

Optional only for pixel_plane: a second [x,y,z] point for the same caller-supplied plane normal. The tool returns alternate_point_m, alternate_ray_distance_m and assumption_delta_m so you can see how the plane hypothesis changes the result; it does not select a default or measure the surface. If either intersection is near-parallel, nonfinite or behind the camera, the query returns unknown/null.

Optional only for pixel_plane: saved calibrated camera in the same observation (such as a wrist view) on which to project point_m (and optional alternate_point_m) and return a geometry overlay image in the same call.

Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. In this run pixel_plane also accepts plane_source:'vggt', which replaces your plane height with an image-based estimate of the object's centre height at that pixel (alternate: its top); check value.plane_estimate.quality. Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. In this run pixel_plane also accepts plane_source:'vggt', which replaces your plane height with an image-based estimate of the object's centre height at that pixel (alternate: its top); check value.plane_estimate.quality. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"cam_head","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}

pool:
Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. In this run the pixel_plane plane height is estimated from the image (VGGT, centre height of the object at the pixel; value.plane_estimate) unless plane_source is 'caller'; a plane_origin_m you pass is kept as the alternate hypothesis (assumption_delta_m). Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"cam_head","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}

Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. In this run the pixel_plane plane height is estimated from the image (VGGT, centre height of the object at the pixel; value.plane_estimate) unless plane_source is 'caller'; a plane_origin_m you pass is kept as the alternate hypothesis (assumption_delta_m). pool.description: Optional for pixel_plane in this run (required with plane_source 'caller'): an explicit [x,y,z] point on your hypothesized infinite plane, in calibration-frame metres (normally env_origin). Without plane_source 'caller' it is reported as the alternate plane against the estimated height. An intersection is not an observed object surface.

Optional only for pixel_plane: 'vggt' (default in this run) sets the plane to the estimated centre height of the object under the pixel (VGGT monocular depth from this RGB image, scaled by the calibration and the table plane; an estimate, not measured depth); 'caller' uses your plane_origin_m/plane_normal unchanged.

pool:
Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. In this run pixel_plane also accepts plane_source:'vggt', which replaces your plane height with an image-based estimate of the object's centre height at that pixel (alternate: its top); check value.plane_estimate.quality. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"cam_head","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}

Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. In this run pixel_plane also accepts plane_source:'vggt', which replaces your plane height with an image-based estimate of the object's centre height at that pixel (alternate: its top); check value.plane_estimate.quality. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"cam_head","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}

Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"cam_head","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}

Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"cam_head","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}

Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"cam_head","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}
